title: A Probabilistic Perspective on Tiling Sparse Tensor Algebra
problem: Tiling sparse tensor algebra computations for cache efficiency is challenging because the effective tile size and cache behavior depend on the sparse data distribution, which varies across inputs and is not known at compile time.
motivation: Sparse tensor operations underlie graph analytics, scientific computing, and machine learning workloads; poor tiling decisions cause cache thrashing and memory bandwidth bottlenecks that significantly limit performance on real hardware.
method: The paper takes a probabilistic approach to sparse tensor tiling, modeling the sparsity pattern probabilistically to predict cache behavior and guide tile-size selection. Specific mechanism details are not available from the abstract alone.
key_novelty: A probabilistic framework for analyzing and selecting tile sizes in sparse tensor algebra that accounts for input-dependent sparsity patterns.
contributions: Probabilistic model for cache behavior of sparse tensor algebra under varying sparsity patterns
Tiling strategy guided by sparsity probability models rather than static heuristics
primary_theme: probabilistic tiling optimization for sparse tensor algebra
